facing_direction.note: Generic Bedrock int facing (buttons, dispenser, dropper, hopper, ladder, barrel, observer pre-1.21). EXCEPTION: piston, sticky_piston and *_piston_arm_collision use 2=south, 3=north, 4=east, 5=west.

minecraft:facing_direction.note: String variant used by observer; same meaning as Java `facing`.

minecraft:cardinal_direction.note: String horizontal facing (chest, furnace, repeater, comparator, fence gate, door). Same names as Java `facing` and the same value for all of these EXCEPT doors, where the J2B data rotates by 90 degrees (see minecraft:oak_door).

weirdo_direction.note: Stairs: direction the full-block (back) side faces = Java stairs `facing`.

direction (trapdoor).note: Trapdoors: value -> Java `facing`. 0 = trapdoor on the west side of its block.

torch_facing_direction.note: Names the attached block face; the torch top points the OPPOSITE way, i.e. Bedrock value = opposite of Java wall_torch `facing`.

rail_direction.note: Same order as Java `shape`; powered/detector/activator rails only 0-5.

lever_direction.note: Wall values = Java facing; floor/ceiling only encode the axis (north/south or east/west), not the 180-degree handle direction.

sources.j2b-1.26.30: https://github.com/PrismarineJS/minecraft-data/blob/master/data/bedrock/1.26.30/blocksJ2B.json (community; Java state -> Bedrock state, Geyser-style, visual-oriented)

propertyKinds.state: Java property maps to a Bedrock block state (see `states`).
propertyKinds.identifier: Java property selects the Bedrock identifier (see `identifierBy`).
propertyKinds.waterLayer: Java `waterlogged`. Bedrock has no state; water is a second block layer (layer 1 = minecraft:water liquid_depth=0) at the same position. In .mcstructure: second `block_indices` array.
propertyKinds.derived: Recomputed by the game from neighbours/redstone; write the Bedrock default and let the world update it.
propertyKinds.blockEntity: Bedrock keeps this in the block entity (`block_entity_data`), not in the block state.
propertyKinds.lost: No Bedrock equivalent; the information is dropped (lossy).

minecraft:corner.note: Added in Bedrock 26.50 (wiki:BE26.50). Values equal Java `shape` except straight -> none. Neighbour updates only in worlds created with base game version >= 1.26.40.

notes: Bedrock id differs for stone_stairs (Bedrock normal_stone_stairs) and cobblestone_stairs (Bedrock stone_stairs): never map by id string alone.
weirdo_direction 0..3 = east, west, south, north; upside_down_bit = Java half=top.

Wool/concrete stairs: Java 26.3; Bedrock 26.40 (experiment 'Drop 3 of 2026', wool) / 26.50 (released, concrete added in 26.50). Not in the 26.30 J2B data: mapping derived from oak_stairs and checked against the 26.60 permutation list (same states as all other stairs).
Bedrock 26.50 bug list: '[Experimental] The new single wool slabs and stairs conduct redstone' (MCPE-240018) - check conductivity before relying on it in redstone builds.
Bedrock uses separate ids for double slabs (`<x>_double_slab`, vertical_half=bottom). Single slab: minecraft:vertical_half = Java type (top/bottom).
Bedrock id differs for stone_slab (Bedrock normal_stone_slab).

Wool/concrete slabs: Java 26.3; Bedrock 26.40 experiment / 26.50 release. Derived from oak_slab, ids `<color>_wool_double_slab` / `<color>_concrete_double_slab` confirmed in wiki ID table and 26.60 permutation list.
wall_connection_type_*: Java low -> short, tall -> tall, none -> none; wall_post_bit = Java up. Bedrock stores these, but they are recomputed from neighbours like in Java.

Fence connection states exist since Bedrock 26.50 (before: no states, computed at render). Connection rules differ: Bedrock fences/panes/walls connect to honey blocks (MCPE-123695) and fences do not connect to glass/glowstone; the game recomputes them on update.
Glass panes / iron bars got minecraft:connection_* states in Bedrock 26.50; neighbour updates only in new worlds.

powered.note: Bedrock has no powered state for fence gates.

notes: Oak fence gate is `minecraft:fence_gate` in Bedrock (other woods `<wood>_fence_gate`).

powered.note: Bedrock has no powered state for doors.

notes: Oak door is `minecraft:wooden_door`.

CONFLICT: J2B maps Java facing north/east/south/west -> minecraft:cardinal_direction east/south/west/north (rotated 90 degrees clockwise); minecraft.wiki describes minecraft:cardinal_direction with the same meaning as Java `facing`. Plausible explanation (assumed): doors kept their legacy `direction` numbering (0 = east, like pre-1.13 Java door metadata) and the 1.21.60 migration to minecraft:cardinal_direction converted the numbers with the generic 0=south/1=west/2=north/3=east table, so the string is offset by 90 degrees. We keep the J2B table (it is used by Geyser clients every day). Verify in-game before B1 ships (place a door facing north, export it as .mcstructure and read the state).
Oak trapdoor is `minecraft:trapdoor`. Still uses int `direction` (0 east, 1 west, 2 south, 3 north = Java facing) - not migrated to minecraft:cardinal_direction as of 26.60.

Oak button is `minecraft:wooden_button`. facing_direction: 0 ceiling, 1 floor, 2..5 wall north/south/west/east. Floor/ceiling buttons have no rotation in Bedrock: Java `facing` for face=floor|ceiling is lost (wiki:Button; parity list: 'Can face in all directions when on the top or bottom of a block' is Java-only).
Oak pressure plate is `minecraft:wooden_pressure_plate`. Java `powered` (bool) -> redstone_signal 15/0.

distance.note: Bedrock leaves have no distance state; decay check uses update_bit (write 0 for persistent leaves).

waterlogged.note: Waterlogged leaves spread water in Bedrock (MCPE-153400), not in Java.

notes: Java `axis` -> Bedrock `pillar_axis`, same values.

waterlogged.note: Rails are destroyed by flowing water in Bedrock.

notes: `powered` -> rail_data_bit. powered_rail is `minecraft:golden_rail`.
Bedrock has only minecraft:air.
Bedrock has only minecraft:air.

facing.note: moving_block block entity: movingBlock, movingBlockExtra, pistonPosX/Y/Z.

notes: Technical block; never exported by the builder (only appears mid-motion).

snowy.note: Bedrock has no snowy state; the side texture is chosen by the renderer.

notes: Same id. Torches/buttons attach to top and sides in Bedrock too (MCPE-17487, Works as Intended); the 'Bedrock differs' comment in registry/data/glass.ts is outdated. Glass passes redstone dust power downward in Bedrock.
Bedrock id `minecraft:snow` (the layer block is `minecraft:snow_layer`).
Bedrock id `minecraft:brick_block`.
Bedrock id `minecraft:hardened_clay` (colored terracotta uses `<color>_terracotta`).
Bedrock quartz_block carries pillar_axis (Java has none): always write `y`.
Bedrock id `minecraft:slime`.
`lit=true` -> `minecraft:lit_furnace`. Furnace contents live in the block entity.

type.note: Double chests: block entity fields pairx/pairz (+ pairlead); without them two adjacent chests may pair or stay single depending on placement.

notes: J2B maps facing with the generic facing_direction table (north=2 ... east=5). The wiki block-state table for barrels lists 2=east,3=west,4=south,5=north, which contradicts both J2B and every other facing_direction table - treated as a wiki error, verify in-game.

waterlogged.note: Waterlogged ladders cannot be climbed in Bedrock (wiki:Ladder).

notes: Floor torch = torch_facing_direction=top.
Bedrock has no separate wall torch id: `minecraft:torch` with torch_facing_direction = opposite of Java facing.
level 0 -> minecraft:water (source), 1..15 -> minecraft:flowing_water with the same liquid_depth. Builds only ever contain sources.
level 0 -> minecraft:lava, 1..15 -> minecraft:flowing_lava.

Connection states added in Bedrock 26.60. NAME CONFLICT: minecraft-data 26.60 permutations call them redstone_north/east/south/west; the wiki copy of the official 26.60 changelog says minecraft:connection_north/... Values none|side|up in both. Verify before writing them; omitting them is safe (the game recomputes connections).
Bedrock dust cannot be a dot: an unconnected wire is always a cross (MCPE-83955). Java `dot` shapes (all none, power irrelevant) become crosses that DO power their neighbours.
Bedrock dust auto-connects to the back/sides of pistons.
`lit=false` -> `minecraft:unlit_redstone_torch` (separate id).
Same id as floor redstone torch, torch_facing_direction = opposite of Java facing; `lit=false` -> unlit_redstone_torch.

open_bit.reason: J2B flips open_bit for floor/ceiling levers with facing south/east to imitate the Java handle direction (visual-only). For a structure that must behave correctly, open_bit = powered (wiki:Lever: 'If the lever is currently activated').

notes: lever_direction combines Java face+facing; for face=floor|ceiling only the axis survives (north=south, east=west): 180-degree handle direction is lost.

locked.note: No state in 26.60; `locked` is upcoming in Bedrock 26.70 (wiki:Redstone_Repeater).

notes: `powered` selects powered_repeater / unpowered_repeater. repeater_delay = Java delay - 1.
`powered` selects powered_/unpowered_comparator AND output_lit_bit. Output signal strength is in the comparator block entity (OutputSignal).

extended.note: Piston block entity (State/NewState/Progress/Sticky). An extended piston also needs the arm block (piston_arm_collision) in front.

notes: facing_direction uses the PISTON table: 0 down, 1 up, 2 south, 3 north, 4 east, 5 west (differs from dispenser/observer).
Same facing table as piston.
`type` selects piston_arm_collision / sticky_piston_arm_collision; piston facing table.
String minecraft:facing_direction = Java facing (observed direction).

toggle_bit.reason: J2B maps enabled=true -> toggle_bit=true, but wiki:Hopper defines toggle_bit=1 as 'hopper cannot move items' (powered). Semantics are inverted to Java `enabled`; we follow the wiki definition.

notes: facing_direction: 0 down, 2..5 north/south/west/east (generic table).
`lit=true` -> `minecraft:lit_redstone_lamp`.
Bedrock id `minecraft:noteblock`, no block states. Changing the note does not cause a block update in Bedrock (MCPE-53919): observers cannot detect it.
`inverted=true` -> `minecraft:daylight_detector_inverted`; power -> redstone_signal.
`unstable` -> explode_bit (only state in 26.60; the Education-only allow_underwater_bit listed on Microsoft Learn is not part of the vanilla 26.60 permutations).

waterlogged.note: Rails are destroyed by flowing water in Bedrock.

notes: Lone rails: Java places them along the player's look direction; this is listed as Java-only in the parity list (MCPE-52823).
